moat_against: Pure commodity price-taker — no pricing power over oil, gas or NGL prices
Reserves deplete — continuous capex required just to hold production flat
AECO/NYMEX basis and takeaway exposure on Montney gas volumes
Long-term energy-transition demand risk for oil and gas
moat_for: Deep premium inventory in Permian (Midland) and Montney — 3,200+ locations added since 2023, plus 930 NuVista locations
Cost leadership: undisputed lowest-cost Montney operator, top-2 lowest cost in the Midland Basin
Highest-productivity oil wells in the Midland Basin and Montney
Infrastructure/processing access adjacent to the Montney position; ~$100M/yr of expected NuVista cost synergies
moat_justification: Weak moat (4/10): real cost and inventory advantages — deep premium drilling inventory in the Permian (Midland) and Montney, cost leadership in the Montney and top-2 lowest costs in the Midland Basin, highest-productivity oil wells in both plays — but Ovintiv is a pure commodity price-taker: oil, gas and NGL prices are set by the market, reserves deplete and must be re-drilled just to hold production flat, and returns are capped by basis differentials, takeaway and the energy transition. Cost leadership survives a cycle; it does not compound like a wide moat. CAP = 7.2 years.
name: Ovintiv Inc.
one_liner: High-quality Permian/Montney E&P, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $66.16 (weighted IRR 13.4%, weighted IV@15 $57.97) because the TTM base embeds an acquisition-overlap period and strong H1 2026 prices; clears 15% at ~$57.97.
